Writer-marked T26 (the heading shares "paranoia" and "warning sign" with the first sentence) is justified, because the echo is how a skimmer finds the case and the sentence says what the heading can't. Linter: "B7 short landing at paragraph end" is a six-word heading read as a paragraph, "D9 follows the source order" is a heading following its own paragraphs by design (T13 and T09 do not apply to a heading), and "E36/E41 heavy second person" counts one "your" in a heading that speaks to the reader as the guide's other headings do, so I accept all three.
